Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — proposed scenarios and unit econ

Samir — thanks, and appreciate the quick confirmation. Per our conversation and your asks, attached are three straightforward reserved-capacity scenarios and high-level unit-econ math. See the attached CSV for throughput assumptions.

Summary (high-level):
Option A — 2x H100-equivalent (baseline)
- Estimated monthly reserved list: $12,000/mo
- Estimated aggregate steady throughput: ~2.0k tok/sec (burst ~2.8k)
- Good for: proof-of-concept and low-to-mid token volumes (up to ~1.5B/mo)
- Unit-econ (example): $12,000 / 1.2B tokens = $10.00 / 1M tokens

Option B — 4x H100-equivalent (recommended initial commit)
- Estimated monthly reserved list: $24,000/mo
- Estimated aggregate steady throughput: ~4.5k tok/sec (burst ~6k)
- Good for: 1.8–3.0B token/mo profiles, headroom for peak slices
- Unit-econ (example): $24,000 / 2.5B tokens = $9.60 / 1M tokens

Option C — 8x A100-equivalent (cost-performance tradeoff)
- Estimated monthly reserved list: $30,000/mo
- Estimated aggregate steady throughput: ~5.0k tok/sec (depends on model & quant)
- Good for: highest throughput with more cost spread across GPUs
- Unit-econ (example): $30,000 / 2.5B tokens = $12.00 / 1M tokens

Notes on assumptions (see throughput-estimates.csv):
- Unit-econ numbers above are pure reserved-cost / token-volume illustrations. They exclude data egress, proactive caching, and per-request tooling fees which we can break out separately.
- Batching, KV-cache hit rate (we assumed ~40% prefix reuse), and quantization (int8/4) materially change throughput and therefore unit cost. We’ll run a quick perf sweep with infra to refine these numbers.
- If your procurement max is $30k/mo, Option B at $24k/mo gives the best mix of throughput and predictable cost; Option C is higher list price but may hit better raw throughput depending on model/tokenization.

Action items
- If these look reasonable, I’ll have Marcus and Dylan run a targeted perf estimate for your representative prompt set and model (can do by EOD tomorrow).
- I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 10/07 10:00am PT and include a short deck with the three scenarios and TCO slides.

Attachments: Initial_Pricing_Estimate_FinLytics.pdf, throughput-estimates.csv

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
